チキンの丸焼きこっころこ.name: Chikin no Maruyaki Kokkoroko
チキンの丸焼きこっころこ.desc: A one-of-a-kind chicken soba made by a whole-roast-chicken specialty shop. Garlicky roast chicken sits boldly on top, and the soup, infused with the fat and aroma of the roast, has a character no other shop has. Keihan (chicken rice) and takeout whole roast chicken too.
t: This article was created with AI (ChatGPT 5 Thinking), with some parts added by me 😁
I ate here in December 2024 😄 Today I visited "Chikin no Maruyaki Kokkoroko" in Awase, Okinawa City.
Chikin no Maruyaki Kokkoroko
Banners outside the shop
The sign and exterior are cute, with wood-grain accents standing out on the white building along the road 🏠 There's a ramp in front of the shop, too, giving it an easy-to-enter feel.
Inside the shop (there's a guitar on display (^0^;))
Inside the shop

When you go inside, the first thing that jumps out at you is the wall of autograph boards above the counter 📸 You can feel how loved it is by locals. When you sit down, the savory smell of roast chicken is already gently tickling your nose, and your appetite switch turns on naturally 😄
Price revision notice
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu

Flip through the menu and, as expected, the star is chicken. A whole roast is ¥2,000, the "tori-zara (half)" to enjoy in the shop is ¥1,200, and the quarter (Kokkoroko Special) is ¥1,000 — a solid lineup. For takeout fans there's also the "Chicken L pack (1/2) ¥1,200" and "S pack (1/4) ¥850", so munching on it at home while watching a movie sounds nice too 🚗 I also discovered a new menu item, "keihan (chicken rice) ¥800". It seems to be an arrangement of the Amami Oshima local dish using their roast chicken, so it's decided as homework for next time 🍗✨
That said, today I came to eat Okinawa soba, so I ordered the "chicken soba" in "large".
Chicken soba (large) ¥880

The bowl that arrived has, as in the photo, roast chicken sitting boldly on top of the soup. The skin is nicely browned, and from the first bite the garlic in the seasoning comes through strongly, with an impact that makes you go "Oh!" 🧄🍜 The clear golden soup is less the sharp, "straight-up clear chicken broth" type and more the type where the fat and aroma of the roast have slowly melted in. Rather than competing on the outline of the broth alone, it pushes forward with the savoriness only a chicken specialty shop can offer. A flavor you can only find here — I kept nodding and my spoon wouldn't stop 😋
Chicken soba (large) ¥880

The noodles are medium-thick and gently wavy. Pale and smooth, cooked on the soft side. Rather than pulling you along with chewiness, they're designed to coat themselves in soup as you slurp. Personally I'd like a bit more bite, but they have a "good receiving quality" that catches the punch of the star chicken and garlic, so the overall flow isn't bad. When you lift the noodles, the aroma spreads softly with the steam, and adding a little green onion lightens the aftertaste. Adding pickled red ginger midway tightens everything up at once, and the heaviness of the second half disappears — that's nice too 🥢

And then the chicken topping. When you put your chopsticks in, it comes apart tenderly along the fibers. The skin is savory, and the inside is moist. As the garlic seasoning blends into the soup, its sharp edges soften and layers of umami build up, which is fun. It's nice that you can reset your palate with the namasu-style side dish and go back to the soup in a loop. Since I went with "large", it's more filling than it looks, and my stomach was well satisfied 🐔

I think what makes this bowl interesting is that it's complete not through "purity of broth" but through "the shop's character". The worldview is clear with three points: the roast aroma, the garlic flavor, and the soft noodles, and if you come expecting the classic pork-bone or bonito-forward Okinawa soba, you'll be betrayed in a good way. Opinions may be divided, but if asked "Can you only eat this here?", I'd proudly answer yes. It hits the spot on days when you want to eat heartily or recharge your stamina after work. If you go along mixing in flavor changes with the pickled red ginger and green onion on the table, you can enjoy it without getting bored until the end. For those who like spicy food, next time I'm curious about the chili sauce suggestion for the "keihan" too 🌶️
A price revision notice was posted in the shop, but I felt a determination of "we'll satisfy you with the volume on the plate" to make up for it.

They also offer takeout and vacuum packs, so it seems handy for family gatherings and as a treat to bring to people 📝 Making "our own chicken soba" at home by preparing a hot soup and topping it with a quarter sounds fun too. There are days for tackling the classic tourist spots, and days like this for dropping casually by a distinctive local shop, and I reflected that both are good ✨

Rating (9/15): All in all, the chicken soba at "Chikin no Maruyaki Kokkoroko" was a bowl that "pulls you along with the deliciousness of the meat", lightly leaping beyond the framework of Okinawa soba. The direction of the soup isn't the easy-to-grasp type, but the savoriness of the roast and the punch of garlic keep you eating right to the end. If you're looking for something distinctive, or it's a day you want to eat well, please give it a try 🍜

ナナチ.name: Nanachi
ナナチ.desc: A new shop whose selling points are Daito soba and Daito sushi. The glossy, chewy, thick wavy aged fresh noodles are delicious in a way no other shop offers. Touch-panel ordering and smartphone payment, and the Daito sushi made with fish shipped straight from the Daito Islands looks tempting too.
t: I went to eat here in May 2023. It recently opened along Prefectural Route 7, which I take to and from my surf point (Itoman City, Suicide Cliff point), so I'd been curious about it 😄
Nanachi, along Prefectural Route 7
The moment I parked in the lot, someone from the shop noticed and even came outside to greet me ^^; Kind of embarrassing ^^;
Looking at the banners outside, maybe they're from Higashi? Minamidaito Island — they seem to be featuring "Daito soba" and "Daito sushi".
Menu (I ate on the terrace seats, where you can feel the outdoor air 😄)

Right when you enter, there's a touch-panel machine, and it's prepay. My impression is that many Okinawa soba shops are still cash-only, but since this one opened recently, I could pay by smartphone 😊 Nice. I wish restaurants would go cashless soon.
This time I ordered the "Nanachi Special (¥1,100)" recommended by the staff, with a large portion of noodles (+¥100).
Nanachi Special (large noodles) ¥1,200

The banner said "aged fresh noodles", and in the soup with a strong pork bone broth, the noodles are thick and wavy — glossy, chewy, and satisfying. Noodles unlike other shops', and delicious 😋 The toppings — pork spare ribs (soki), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), fish cake (kamaboko), pickled red ginger, and green onion — were chosen on the touch panel.

Rating (10/15): The thick wavy aged fresh noodles were delicious even compared to other shops. The toppings and soup are simply tasty. However, I paid +¥100 for large noodles, but the amount didn't really feel like a large portion, and the price may be a bit high compared to other shops. (Then again, maybe other shops are too cheap ^^;)
The cute ball-shaped(?) Daito sushi apparently uses fish shipped directly from the Daito Islands, and the photo on the menu looked delicious 🤤

パパイヤとスブイ.name: Papaya to Subui
パパイヤとスブイ.desc: Creative Okinawa soba with distinctive shiitake broth and papaya and subui (winter melon) toppings. After Ishikawa in Uruma City and Matsuo in Naha City, it now operates inside Ginowan Yui Marche. The Lemosco condiment is something other shops don't have.
t: ― 3rd visit (May 2025, Ginowan Yui Marche) ―
I ate here in May 2025 😆 This time on my Okinawa soba tour, I went to "Ginowan Yui Marche" in Oyama, Ginowan City.
Ginowan Yui Marche
Papaya to Subui (inside Ginowan Yui Marche)
Papaya to Subui

Inside the marche, lined with local vegetables and souvenirs, is "Papaya to Subui no Okinawa Soba". From outside, the bright yellow-green sign catches your eye, and it has a somewhat quirky atmosphere — you'd never think there was an Okinawa soba shop inside a marche.
Inside the shop
Inside the shop

I'd eaten at Papasubu before at the Uruma City location and the location in front of the Prefectural Office, but this was my first visit in quite a long time. There's a ticket machine at the front, and it's lined with Okinawa soba you rarely see elsewhere, starting with Papasubu soba, plus sunui shiitake soba, shikuwasa wasabi soba, ume and ginger soba, squid ink soba, and more. A lineup that's exciting for anyone who wants to enjoy creative Okinawa soba, different from the standard sanmai-niku soba or soki soba.
Meal ticket machine
Meal ticket machine
That day, the blackboard in the shop said "¥200 cashback for customers ordering vegetable soba", so I ordered the limited-time recommendation, "vegetable soba", without hesitation.
The vegetable soba was a good deal today 😆

Looking at the photo, it's piled high with leafy green stems, eggplant, green pepper, bell pepper, kombu, and more, and it looks quite hearty. On top of that there's chopped meat and bonito flakes too, so the bowl is lively 😊
Vegetable soba ¥1,050 (*¥850 with the ¥200 cashback)

When I first drank the soup, the flavor was quite different from the usual Okinawa soba pork bone or bonito broth. Maybe it's shiitake broth — a soup with a distinctive aroma and umami, light but with a strong character. If you're expecting the bonito aroma typical of Okinawa soba, you might be a little surprised. Perhaps the moisture from the vegetables was added too, but overall it was a gentle flavor, and I found it a bit lacking.

The vegetables are also quite different from a typical vegetable soba. The main ones were summer vegetables like leafy green stems, eggplant, green pepper, and bell pepper. The seasoning is very restrained — the type where you enjoy the vegetables' own aroma and texture. I think it's a bowl vegetable lovers will enjoy.
Vegetable soba ¥1,050 (*¥850 with the ¥200 cashback)
The noodles are said to be homemade hand-kneaded noodles — medium-thin and wavy. A bit on the thin side for Okinawa soba noodles.

The chopped meat on top was also something quite different from the usual Okinawa soba braised pork belly or pork spare ribs. Maybe a five-spice-like aroma — a distinctive seasoning that also felt a bit herbal, another flavor you rarely encounter at other shops. Both the soup and the toppings gave the impression of being finished as tropical-style creative cuisine rather than leaning toward the Okinawa soba standard. When I added a harissa-like condiment midway, a curry-like spiciness came out, and it changed into an even more ethnic-leaning bowl 🌶️

Honestly, in terms of my personal taste, the flavor didn't really click for me. Overall it was lightly seasoned, and quite different in direction from the powerful pork bone or bonito I look for in Okinawa soba. However, there really are a lot of vegetables, and by the time you finish you'll be quite full. I think it's an interesting shop for people who want to eat plenty of vegetables, people looking for an unusual variety different from the usual Okinawa soba, and people who like spicy or creative flavors.

Rating (9.5/15): Being inside Ginowan Yui Marche, it's easy to drop by while shopping, which is nice. If you want to feel the breadth of Okinawa soba, I'd really like you to try Papasubu's one-of-a-kind Okinawa soba at least once ✨
― 2nd visit (October 2024, Matsuo, Naha City) ―

I ate here in October 2024 😆 This time I visited "Okinawa Soba Papaya to Subui" in Matsuo, Naha City. I'd been once before when it was in Ishikawa, Uruma City, but this is my first visit since it moved to Naha City.
Okinawa Soba Papaya to Subui

The shop is on the 1st floor of an old building, and when you go inside, a calm space with lots of houseplants spreads out, with an atmosphere just like a café 😊 Elementary school tables and chairs are used, which I felt helped create a cozy feel.
Inside the shop (recycled elementary school tables and chairs 😄)
Inside the shop (recycled elementary school tables and chairs 😄)
A whole "subui (winter melon)", from the shop's name, is placed as interior decor 😆

When I checked the menu on the meal ticket machine near the entrance, there was a range of creative Okinawa soba. Among them, the signature "Papasubu soba" caught my interest. I bought a ticket and waited at a table surrounded by plants. There were several other customers in the shop besides me, and everyone seemed to be spending a leisurely time.
Meal ticket machine near the entrance

While waiting in the shop, I looked out the window and it was raining. But somehow the atmosphere of this rainy day felt pleasant. The green of the houseplants, the old-fashioned furniture, and the natural light coming through the windows blend together in perfect balance 😌
After a while, the "Papasubu soba" was brought out in a yellow bowl.
Papasubu soba ¥900

First, as usual, I start with the soup. One sip, and a deep flavor unlike the Okinawa soba shops so far spreads out. In addition to pork, chicken, and bonito, the broth made from plenty of shiitake is its distinctive feature.

Actually, I felt this soup was delicious enough to work as a ramen soup rather than an Okinawa soba one. The strong shiitake flavor was especially memorable, a deep taste where you can also sense elements of Japanese dashi. This is a unique worldview you can hardly find at other shops 😋
Papasubu soba ¥900

The noodles are homemade hand-kneaded noodles with a gentle wave, and they have a moderate chewiness. They cling well to the soup, and eating them together seems to bring out the soup's umami even more. The thickness is about medium-thin, I'd say. The firmness is just right, and they kept a good texture right to the end.

The toppings, shibui and braised pork belly, are slowly simmered until melt-in-your-mouth tender. However, the braised pork belly still had a slightly sinewy quality, which bothered me a little. There's plenty of green onion on top, and eating it mixed with the soup adds a nice accent.
Papasubu soba ¥900

What was interesting was the condiment on the table. Instead of kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori), the usual Okinawa soba condiment, there was "Lemosco". It's a spicy condiment made with Setouchi lemons, and when I tried adding it to the soup, a nice sourness and heat were added, changing it into a completely new flavor! I was impressed by what a novel idea this is 😆
Lemosco (a condiment other shops don't have)

The way the atmosphere is created is distinctive too — the wooden tables like old school desks and the arrangement of houseplants seem to deliberately create a nostalgic space. A big houseplant is placed by the window, and beyond it you can see the kitchen. Every so often a lovely aroma of broth being made drifted from the kitchen, which whetted my appetite.

Rating (10.5/15): As a creative Okinawa soba, I felt it was a bowl with its own unique worldview. The distinctive soup with a strong shiitake flavor in particular is an appeal other shops don't have. It's wonderful that they've kept the same flavor even after moving to Naha City. Including the atmosphere of the shop, I think it's a valuable place where you can enjoy Okinawa soba at a relaxed pace.
― 1st visit (March 2023, Ishikawa, Uruma City) ―
*The following is an article from when it operated in Ishikawa, Uruma City. It has now moved to Ginowan City.
In March 2023 I went to "Papaya to Subui", located pretty much along Route 329.
Papaya to Subui — a stylish exterior, isn't it

This shop, which opened on April 11, 2022 in a renovated former ramen shop — I learned from TV or somewhere that they use papaya and subui, and shiitake for the soup broth, so I'd been curious about it.

"Papaya" seems to be a tropical fruit native to tropical America, but in Okinawa the green unripe fruit (green papaya) is eaten as a vegetable. In Okinawan cuisine it's often eaten as papaya champuru ☺ It's delicious.
"Subui" is winter melon (togan), a vegetable native to tropical Asia and a staple of Okinawan cuisine. This is delicious too.
From the meal ticket machine, I ordered the "Papasubu soba", whose name suggests these are used as toppings.
Papasubu soba ¥830 — the bowls and everything are stylish too.

In a very stylish atmosphere inside the shop, first I took a sip of the soup 😀 Mmm, as expected it's different from the soups at other shops so far, and refreshing. Apparently, in addition to bonito, kombu, pork, and chicken broth, the soup is made from a large amount of shiitake and seasoned with Okinawan salt and sukugarasu. The homemade hand-kneaded noodles cling to the soup and are delicious 😋

The toppings are tender pork and, though it's hidden in the photo, melt-in-your-mouth subui (winter melon) soaked with flavor. There's also bonito flakes, papaya, julienned kombu, and shiitake, unique toppings you can't find at other shops, which is refreshing too. Healthy, isn't it.

Rating (10.5/15): The exterior and interior are very stylish, and the woman of the young tourist couple at the table next to me was really delighted 😀 Like, coming here was the right call lol. The hand-kneaded wavy noodles are delicious, and the toppings really are different from other shops, so it's refreshing. How about it, for those who are tired of regular Okinawa soba?

PS: However, I'm sorry to say, even though they went to the trouble of stylishly renovating the building and interior, the toilet in the separate building was old inside and not very clean, which I thought was a shame.

沖縄そば屋FLOG（ふろっぐ）.name: Okinawa Sobaya FLOG (Furoggu)
沖縄そば屋FLOG（ふろっぐ）.desc: A shop in Ohigashi, Nago City, also featured on the TV program "Uchiran". An all-too-unique style with a golf simulator inside and daytime drinking OK. The Okinawa soba is an orthodox bonito broth.
t: This time I'm introducing "Okinawa Sobaya FLOG (Furoggu)" in Ohigashi, Nago City! I went to eat here in February 2025 😄
FLOG (Furoggu)
FLOG (Furoggu)
FLOG (Furoggu)
This shop was actually featured on the TV program "Uchiran" ✨ Since it had been featured, I got curious and went~!

The shop's exterior is a building with a striking red awning, and "Okinawa soba" banners are put up along the road, so it's easy to spot even while driving. Near the entrance there's a blackboard sign, handwritten with "Okinawa soba — open now", and also "Daytime drinking available 🍺". An Okinawa soba shop where you can drink from noon is pretty rare, isn't it 😄
Inside the shop (you can play golf (^0^;))
Inside the shop (you can play golf (^0^;))

When you go inside... the first thing that jumps out at you is a golf simulator 😅 No, really, it's a space where you can actually play golf inside the shop. There were golf bags, and simulator footage was being projected by a projector. Golf while eating Okinawa soba!? That's quite a unique combination lol. There are also TV screens and counter seats in the shop, and there's a somewhat bar-like atmosphere too. The direction of enjoying drinks from lunchtime came through clearly 😊
Menu
Menu

The menu is simple: sanmai-niku soba (medium ¥800 / large ¥880), nankotsu soki soba (medium ¥800 / large ¥880), mixed soba (large ¥950), and jushi (small ¥200 / large ¥300). For drinks, they have everything from sanpin tea, cola, and iced coffee (¥300) to beer and highballs (¥600) — well stocked to suit the daytime drinking style 🍺
This time I ordered the "mixed soba (large) (¥950)". A greedy bowl where you can enjoy both braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs!
Mixed soba (large) ¥950

Looking at the soba brought out after a while, it's piled with plenty of green onion, with braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs lined up beneath. It looks quite hearty 😋 First, a sip of the soup. An orthodox soup with a solid bonito broth.
Mixed soba (large) ¥950

Next I have the noodles. Medium-thick and straight, with a softish texture. Both toppings, the braised pork belly and the soft-bone pork ribs, are moderately infused with flavor, and still have a bit of a sinewy texture.

By the way, as for the customers other than me... everyone was eating set meals with grilled fish! The aroma of grill-roasted fish drifted through the shop, and it looked so delicious, yassa 🐟 Maybe grilled fish is their signature dish. Maybe the grilled fish set meal is more popular than the Okinawa soba? lol. I thought next time I come I'd like to try the grilled fish set meal.
Ume-flavored pickles were served on the table, and they were delicious as a palate cleanser 😄 The refreshing ume flavor was a welcome touch between bites of soba.

Rating (9/15): All in all, the Okinawa soba is orthodox and simply tasty. It's a unique shop with the surprising character of an interior where you can play golf, and you can drink during the day too. When you stop by the Nago area, why not visit once, combined with an unusual experience 😊

ブラジル食堂.name: Burajiru Shokudo
ブラジル食堂.desc: A shop along Prefectural Route 84 near Nago Pineapple Park. The menu is unique, like an "Okinawa soba VS Brazilian cuisine" showdown. You can enjoy light pork-bone soki soba as well as Brazilian-style roast pork, pastel, and more.
t: It was featured on the "Nago City Soba Map", and I ate here in October 2020 😄
Burajiru Shokudo (pretty much along Prefectural Route 84)
"Burajiru Shokudo" is featured as shop 33 of 41 on the "Nago Soba Map"
I ordered the "soki soba" featured on the map. The menu layout is unique, like an "Okinawa soba VS Brazilian cuisine" showdown lol
The unique menu (Okinawa soba VS Brazilian cuisine) 😄
Soki soba (large) ¥700
The soup is a light, pork-bone-based type. The noodles are regular noodles. The soki is also simply tasty.

Rating (9/15): I think it's simply tasty. The location is near tourist spots like "Nago Pineapple Park", so how about it when sightseeing? I didn't take a photo, but inside, someone's soccer uniform was on display 😀

三丁目そば.name: Sanchome Soba
三丁目そば.desc: A shop full of local customers that I happened upon on a back street off Kokusai-dori. Pork bone × bonito blended soup with jiggly soft-bone pork ribs, and amazingly jushi included, all for ¥650 — great value. A pretty high-level bowl.
t: I ate here in June 2023 😄
"Sanchome Soba" — I happened upon it while walking off Kokusai-dori 😊

I had an errand at "Pallet Kumoji", at the end of Kokusai-dori, so I parked in a paid parking lot in a nearby building and walked toward Asato looking for a soba shop, and when I searched the streets behind Kokusai-dori, I found this shop by chance 😄
It's nice, kind of a once-in-a-lifetime encounter (^_^;)

Okinawa had entered the rainy season, but this time there was little rain, and that day was super hot too, and since I'd walked a bit from Pallet Kumoji, I went into the shop drenched in sweat. The shop was cooled pretty strongly, which was the best 😁
Menu posted on the wall
Looking at the menu, I thought that apart from the "Sanchome soba", things were relatively reasonable compared to other shops. The clientele also seems to be mostly locals.
I ordered the "nankotsu soki soba".
Nankotsu soki soba ¥650
Looking at the menu, I thought it was just the soba, but amazingly it also came with jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) — a happy surprise 😆

I felt like starting with the rice, but first, the ritual sip of the soup. The soup looks a bit cloudy, but it's a delicious soup that seems to be a blend with pork bone broth, with a bonito base coming through a little 😋

The noodles are thin and straight, on the soft side. The soft-bone pork ribs are jiggly and infused with flavor — can't go wrong. Delicious 😄 I put them on top of the jushi like a pork bowl and ate it that way, and it was the best lol

Rating (10/15): Simply tasty. I thought it was a pretty high level 😄 It's close to Kokusai-dori, so how about it when you come shopping or sightseeing? I think it's reasonable and delicious Okinawa soba.
*The shop has no parking lot, so you'll need to park at a coin parking lot in the area.
